role: struct env: every piece of state the tick mutates that no world or replay dimension carries (the modules' installed values and counters, vanilla's shared-object state, the survival module's world view, the nbt allocator, the item tag store, the tick scratch) plus the run configuration (the harness switches), reached through the thread-local nw_env.

structs.name: env_scratch
structs.java: World.lightUpdateBlockList and the other buffers a call fills and drains

structs.name: env
structs.java: the per-world-server and static state of one game (one environment)

gpu: about 15.6 MB per environment, most of it the item tag store (6.6 MB), the client particles (surv_fx, 7.8 MB) and the tick scratch; zeroed memory is untouched until used (the first environment is .bss, env_new callocs)
the installed values are pointers into worlds, pools and the replay (Randoms, Det states, callbacks with void * contexts): a device copy needs them as indices
nw_env is a thread-local pointer: one read per access; a device kernel would take the environment from its block index instead
struct bwl (blockwl.h), the block callbacks' frame stack: BWL_CAP 4096 frames of 192 bytes (786 KB, untouched past the deepest point: 895 in a populate spring cascade, 636 in a replay)

scratch.stack (envstack.h): the tick's big locals, ENVSTACK_CAP 256 KB, 105,536 bytes deepest over every test (make -C csrc worklist-depth); make -C csrc stack keeps every tick frame at most 4 KB and each tick root's worst chain under 32 KB
notes: A file reads its fields under the names its globals had: a file static became a #define to its field where it was declared, and the names several files share are defined at the end of env.h. csrc/tests/globals.sh (make globals, run by make test) fails on any writable global outside csrc/tests/globals.allow. Lane gpuphase (GPU audit L6): struct env holds the phase tracer (struct phase_env, phase.h). lane/coldaudit: struct env_scratch is what a call fills and drains (the light pass's queue World.lightUpdateBlockList, the memos under their own stamps, the envstack); nw_scratch is the thread's own copy (nw_thread_scratch, a pool worker's: one warm copy a worker instead of a cold one an environment) or else the environment's (single-world tools, the device build).
